items.question: Can I choose my own body shop, or do I have to use the one my insurance company suggests?
items.answer: You choose. In Alabama the vehicle owner decides where the repair is done. Your insurance company can recommend a shop, but it cannot require one. Tell the adjuster you are using Mac Auto & Collision and we take it from there.

items.question: Do I need more than one estimate?
items.answer: No. One estimate from us is all the claim needs. We write it, send it to your insurance company and handle any follow-up questions from the adjuster.

items.question: Do you work with my insurance company?
items.answer: Yes. We work with every carrier, including State Farm, Allstate, Progressive, GEICO, USAA and Alfa. Bring your claim number if you have one; if you have not filed yet, we can walk you through it.

items.question: How long will the repair take?
items.answer: It depends on the damage and on parts. Small repairs are often two to three days. Major collision work can take one to three weeks. We give you a time estimate up front and call you if anything changes.

items.question: My car can't be driven. Can you help get it to the shop?
items.answer: Yes. Call us at (205) 746-1847 and we will help arrange towing to the shop.

items.question: What if I'm paying out of pocket instead of using insurance?
items.answer: That is fine. We give you an honest written price and repair options that fit your budget, with no claim involved.

items.question: Will the new paint match the rest of my car?
items.answer: Yes. We match the factory color code and blend the new finish into the surrounding panels so the repair is not visible.

items.question: Do you do mechanical work too?
items.answer: Yes. Oil changes, front-end alignments and the mechanical repairs that often come with a collision, such as suspension, steering and cooling components, are done in-house.

items.question: What should I bring to the estimate?
items.answer: Your driver's license, your insurance card, your claim number if you have one, and the vehicle. If the vehicle cannot be driven, photos of the damage are enough to get started.

items.question: The insurance company already sent me an estimate. Do I have to use it?
items.answer: No. That estimate is a starting point, not the final word. Bring it to us. We inspect the whole car, document anything the estimate missed, and send the insurer the difference. That's called a supplement, and it's normal.

items.question: Why is the insurance company's estimate so low?
items.answer: Many first estimates are now written by software from a few photos, before anyone opens a door or lifts a panel. Hidden damage isn't in that number. A real inspection almost always finds more.

items.question: Can I just keep the insurance check and not fix the car?
items.answer: You can, but that first estimate was written to be low, so you may be leaving money and a safe repair on the table. Let us look at the car before you decide. The estimate is free and we'll come to you.

items.question: What does "on-site estimate" mean?
items.answer: We come to wherever the car is: your driveway, your workplace, or the tow yard, anywhere within 40 miles of Bessemer, at no charge. Call (205) 746-1847 to set a time. You get a written estimate on the spot without taking time off to drive to a shop.

items.question: Can you help with my deductible?
items.answer: Ask us how to reduce your deductible. Depending on your policy and the repair, we can often lower what you pay out of pocket, and we finance deductibles in-house. Every situation is different, so the honest answer is a short conversation before any work starts.

items.question: Do you take care of business and fleet vehicles?
items.answer: Yes, and we want more of them. Commercial and fleet accounts are a big part of the shop. We come to your lot for estimates, can pick up and deliver, and keep your paperwork straight. Call and ask about a fleet account.
